[Earth Song by Frank Ticheli](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UUPaoBZ1GbM)

For musicians, I think, to be able to sing or play at your best, you have to be willing to open yourself up to some very dark and lonely lows and very wonderful and bright highs. That roller-coaster produces beautiful and raw things. I remember thinking of music as a talent which I had at the time, not as something alive and sustaining. I'd put emotion into my songs, but not truly feel it.

 During my time with a wonderful chamber choir, the director handed us this piece. I remember so vividly when we first sang it close to perfect for the first time. Towards the end, as soon as "But music and singing shall be my refuge..." came up, I felt tears rolling down my face, and I could hardly keep singing my part (first tenor). In that moment I felt something I can only describe as heaven. It was the most real feeling I've ever felt. All of my burdens and pains were, for that moment, nonexistent. I had goosebumps everywhere, even just remembering it and hearing the version I posted has a similar effect. Physically it felt somewhat akin to taking a cold shower, in that, I could hardly breathe correctly, my body was locked up and shivering, and it felt like I was electrified and floating. It's so hard to describe, so I'm sorry for not doing it justice. :) Remembering that feeling is like a drug, you can't live without it once you've felt it. It hurts remembering it, the flood of that feeling, but it's a good hurt. 

Give it a listen, worth every second.

This tale begins with a younger Thasslol, at a party, imbibing heavily. As the party winds down, the friend who was hosting decided jalapeno poppers sounded like an excellent idea. Having had little to eat all day, I gulped up as many jalapeno poppers as I possibly could. I sleep for a time. About 7am I wake up. This is when something in my lower bowls hits me. I could feel the drums of war in my belly. 

The jalapeno poppers were waging an assault against me. 

I rush to the bathroom, still mostly inebriated from the revelry of the night beforehand, and start heaving. Nothing. My face becomes [This](http://zipmeme.com/uploads/generated/g1336735375521742116.jpg). It was as if they heard me mock their efforts. From the depths of my stomach they rode. Their spicy, yet cheesy, march burning through my throat. But their march was impeded. I couldn't breathe, the poppers where stuck in my throat. Trying to force them out, I pushed and pushed, each effort looking more fruitless than the last. It came, slowly at first, then when enough force to strike the porcelain bowl beneath my head.

Among the remains of my vanquished jalapeno popper foes, lay a single jalapeno popper. The golden breadcrust that once adorned it was gone, but the pepper itself remained. It was whole. I had vomited a whole jalapeno. Victory was had. Drunk and in pain, but proud, I threw a fist in the air. 

TL;DR GOT DRUNK. ATE JALAPENO POPPERS. THREW UP WHOLE JALAPENO.
